title: Maine Coon Kitten's Giant Sasquatch Paws Are Almost Too Cute
content:
Eve Vawter

Sun, November 8, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC

This little Maine Coon kitten has the face of an angel, the prettiest blue eyes, and four feet that look like they belong to an entirely different animal. Seriously, who approved this combination? He’s barely bigger than a loaf of bread, but apparently he’s already preparing to walk through six feet of snow.

And the funniest part is that he looks completely unaware of how ridiculous his paws are. He’s just hanging there being adorable while the rest of us are trying to figure out whether those are kitten feet or miniature snowshoes. I have a Maine Coon named Meatball, and I can absolutely picture him looking at this baby and thinking, “Yep, those are going to be a problem.”

The amazingly floofy little guy appears in a video shared by @mainecoo2, and good grief, he’s cute. His mostly white fur has little patches of orange, his ears are already enormous, and those pink toe beans are practically begging for their own photo shoot.

But it’s the paws that steal the show. They’re so big and fluffy that they almost look like he’s wearing slippers three sizes too large. Somebody needs to tell this kitten that he doesn’t have to grow into his entire adult body by Tuesday.

Related: Blue-Eyed Maine Coon Kitten Looks Like a Scoop of Cookies and Cream With Whiskers

Maine Coons are famous for their impressive size, and those oversized paws are part of what makes the breed so recognizable. Adult males can weigh 15 to 25 pounds or more, although plenty of Maine Coons fall outside that range.

And unlike many other cats, Maine Coons can take several years to reach their full size. So if this little guy’s feet are any indication, somebody might want to start shopping for a bigger cat tree.

How to Groom a Maine Coon

All that gorgeous Maine Coon fluff comes with a little responsibility. These cats have long, thick coats that need regular attention, especially around their bellies, legs, and those spectacular fluffy tails. Sadly, I have not mastered how to groom my own giant fur baby, so I take him somewhere. But if you’d like to groom your own Maine Coon at home, keep reading.

A few grooming basics include:

  • Brush your Maine Coon several times a week to prevent tangles and mats.

  • Pay special attention to the armpits, belly, and behind the ears.

  • Check between those giant toes for dirt or anything caught in the fur.

  • Introduce grooming early so kittens get comfortable being brushed.

And don’t forget regular nail trims. Those adorable Sasquatch feet come equipped with claws.

Honestly, this kitten looks like he’s going to grow into one magnificent cat. But right now, he’s basically a cotton ball wearing snowshoes.
